data.title: 5 out of 5 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Netflix (NFLX) and Meta Platforms (META).

The communications services sector (XLC) lost over 8% so far this year, compared to the nearly 12% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, five tickers reported results, all of which reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, four companies exceeded revenue expectations, while one company trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Netflix (NFLX) shares closed 5% lower on Wednesday following a weaker-than-expected revenue outlook. The streaming giant reported third-quarter revenue of $12.9B, in line with Wall Street estimates, but forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $13.4B, below analysts’ expectations.

Similarly, Meta Platforms (META) slipped 7% after the company’s third-quarter results. Meta’s Q3 earnings showed an increase of 26% in revenues over the past year to a record high of $64.6B. However, its costs and expenses showed an increase of 68% year-over-year. The company now expects to spend $135B to $145B on capital expenditures, increasing the lower end from $130B but remaining within estimates of $138B in capex.

Investors were also disappointed after AT&T’s (T) postpaid phone subscriber additions for the third quarter came in below expectations. Even though the telecom company reported revenue and adjusted earnings above consensus estimates, shares still closed over 6% lower on Wednesday.

For the upcoming week, Alphabet (GOOG), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile US (TMUS) are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Eli Lilly releases promising early-stage data on ADC for ovarian cancer
data.description:
• Phase 1 data on Eli Lilly's (LLY) sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) found that the antibody-drug conjugate plus Avastin (bevacizumab) led to high objective response and disease control rates in individuals with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.
  • Results showed that the combo led to a 79% confirmed objective response rate and 100% disease control rate. Similac reponses were seen across folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression levels.
  • Participants had a median of three prior systemic regimens.
  • The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were epistaxis, nausea, anemia, neutropenia, and fatigue. The most common Grade ≥3 TEAEs were neutropenia and anemia.
  • The FRAmework-01 program is examining the FRα antibody-drug conjugate in both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in three phase 3 trials: Part A as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus Avastin in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARP inhibitor (PARPi); and Part C examines Sofe-M plus Avastin in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway, Blackstone in gainers; HSBC, Globe Life among losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 0.68% from the previous week to close at $55.90.

Among megacap stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD) led the weekly gainers, adding 3.51% to close at $124.61.

The week saw the Canadian lender's U.S. unit launch TD Credit Assist, an AI capability that reduces the time required to prepare a first-draft commercial credit analysis from up to three working days to less than 30 minutes.

"By reducing time spent on manual preparation, our credit professionals can focus more of their time on understanding the client, assessing risk, and moving opportunities forward," said Jill Gateman, Head of Commercial Banking, TD Bank U.S.

Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) (BRK.B) followed with 1.95% and 1.91% gains to $813,595.00 and $542.19, respectively.

B shares touched a new high on Wednesday, an indication that investors have become more confident in Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett as CEO on Jan. 1, 2026.

HSBC Holdings (HSBC) was the top decliner, retreating 4.11% to $90.68.

The global lender is set to post its third-quarter financial results next week; and even as earnings are expected to come in strong on the back of higher interest rates and resilient Asian wealth management fees, mounting cost pressures and regulatory uncertainty from China may impact stock prices.

Japanese lender Mitsubishi UFJ (MUFG) (-3.70% W/W to $21.07) was the next on the list.

The week saw Japanese banks, along with other organizations, temporarily take digital services offline in response to certain security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Separately, the Bank of Japan warned of rising risks from AI, including growing cybersecurity threats and potential ‌market shocks, that could impact the country's banking system.

Globe Life (GL) was among the top largecap losers, retreating 8.28% week-over-week to $154.79.

The life and health insurer was downgraded to Neutral from Overweight at Piper Sandler after reporting third-quarter earnings below Wall Street estimates this week.

First Citizens Bancshares (FCNCA) led the gainers, advancing 11.87% to $2,375.84. The stock was gaining after posting better-than-expected Q3 earnings and announcing a new $1.2B stock buyback program.

Blackstone (BX) added 10.66% from the prior week to $117.97 even as Q3 earnings fell short of consensus.

TransUnion (TRU) (+9.99% W/W to $81.48) extended gains from the previous week, when a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.

Among midcap stocks, UWM Holdings (UWMC) (+38.10% W/W to $1.45) was the top advancer. The mortgage finance provider reported its preliminary unaudited results for the quarter ended September 30, as part of which it said it expects to report total revenue between $800M and $825M, above the consensus of $651.35M.

FirstCash Holdings (FCFS) (-19.75% W/W to $172.75) was the top loser in the category despite a Q3 beat and dividend raise. 

Better Home & Finance (BETR) (+68.04% W/W to $16.72), Chaince Digital (CD) (+26.41% W/W to $8.76), Stewart Information Services (STC) (-16.12% W/W to $44.07), and Gemini Space Station (GEMI) (-14.29% W/W to $3.06) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: Revenge of the consumer: Walmart's $120 bundle takes on Amazon and Costco
data.description:
Walmart (WMT) unveiled a bundled Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus membership option this week in a direct challenge to Amazon Prime (AMZN) and Costco (COST). The joint membership costs $120 per year, which is a saving of $100 per year. It's also $19 cheaper than an annual Amazon Prime membership at $139 and $10 cheaper than Costco's $130 Executive membership but $55 more than Costco's $65 Gold Star membership. The biggest savings are for shoppers who now pay for both Prime and a Costco Executive membership, who would save $149 a year by switching to the bundle.

"This is a direct shot at Prime," United National Consumer Suppliers CEO Brett Rose told Retail Dive. He noted that at $120 per year a member gets a warehouse club, delivery, streaming, and gas thrown in. On paper, Walmart wins the value math easily, highlighted Rose.

“The timing tells you everything. Consumers are stretched heading into the holidays, and memberships lock in loyalty and recurring revenue before the spending gets decided,” Rose said. “Loyalty programs are what keep people coming back. However, not more so than lower prices.”

On Wall Street, Oppenheimer analyst Rupesh Parikh and his team believe consumers are the clear winners from the development due to the stronger combination of perks, the ability to have Walmart and Sam’s Club products delivered to your home with no markups, and minimal incremental costs to upgrade. "This new offering further strengthens Walmart's membership value proposition vs. Amazon Prime and COST. To the extent this membership program takes off, WMT should enjoy incremental wallet share gains, especially on the delivery front, but there is a likely initial P&L headwind near term," advised Parikh.

Looking ahead, the timing of the Walmart (WMT) just ahead of the holidays could put incremental pressure on Amazon (AMZN) and Costco (COST) to dial up promotional activity.

data.title: Iran in 'advanced stages' of plans to target US officials in Middle East
data.description:
• US intelligence has information that Iran is in the 'advanced stages' of plots targeting government officials in the Middle East and beyond, according to a memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.
  • "Specifically, through various channels, we have received intelligence that Iran has substantiallyincreased efforts to target U.S. personnel," Clayton's memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, dated Oct. 23 and obtained by Axios, reads. 
  • Clayton noted he will try to downgrade as much intelligence as he can so Rubio can share the information as widely as possible with personnel who may be impacted.
  • The memo comes following a report in The New York Times on Oct. 21 that the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. 
  • In late September, a Wall Street Journal report said that Trump told advisors he wants to resume bombing after the midterms.

data.title: Vibe Theft Auto: Anthropic Opus, GTA 6, and a potential fade trade
data.description:
The adoption of AI around the video game industry is accelerating, which is raising new opportunities for publishers on the development end, but also creating risks around AI-enabled game recompilation and decompilation. Anthropic's (ANTHRO) latest released Opus version sent a shockwave in the video game sector as it opened up investors to the concept that platform-locked games are portable and games can be easily decompiled.

Vibe coding, which is the practice of describing what you want to an AI model in plain language and letting it write, test, and fix the code, became a major topic after the release of Opus 5.5. That led to some video game stocks selling off amid increased concerns that AI agents can take a shipped game and reconstruct it, turning what was once years of volunteer reverse engineering into days or even hours. 

Digging into the development, Oppenheimer analyst Martin Yang pointed to more than 20 high-profile decompiling projects between mid-September and mid-October. In one case a fleet of AI agents rebuilt the 2009 shooter Modern Warfare 2 from its executable, reaching 99% of functions reconstructed. In other cases, new games saw free copycat versions pop up. "Given the rapid AI model release cadence from leading labs, we see rising AI-headline selloff risks in gaming," he warned.

However, where there is fear, there is also opportunity. Roblox (RBLX) was singled out as resistant to left-tail risks from AI and expected to be an AI benefiiciary.

Looking to the upcoming release of Take-Two Interactive's (TTWO) Grand Theft Auto 6, Yang pointed out that investors could fade any unwarranted, headline-driven share price sell-offs tied to a source code leak or jailbroken version of the highly anticipated game.

Yang highlighted that in a sea of AI slop games, Take-Two Interactive's (TTWO) games will always stand out for their attention to detail and crafted storytelling. "The server-dependent experiences such as GTA Online are less directly exposed to executable copying," he added. 

Related video game ETFs include the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO), the Global X Video Games & Esports ETF (HERO), the Amplify Video Game Leaders ETF (GAMR), and the Roundhill Video Games ETF (NERD), with the Invesco Next Gen Media and Gaming ETF (GGME) as a broader gaming and media fund.

Instacart gains on report it's in talks to sell itself (update)
data.description:
Update 7:48pm: Adds Bloomberg reporting that Uber ended talks with Instacart.

Instacart (CART) jumped 9.2% on a report that the grocery store delivery company is in discussions to try to sell itself.

Instacart (CART) has been working with an investment bank to consider its options and has had preliminary discussions with DoorDash (DASH) and Uber (UBER),  according to a report from The Information on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. Talks are ongoing and there's no guarantee that any deal will happen.

While Instacart (CART) tried to sell itself to Uber (UBER), the ride-hailing firm recently walked away from talks, according to a  Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited a person familiar with the matter. The companies are no longer in discussions.

Instacart has a market cap of $12 billion, while DoorDash is valued at more than $80 billion, and Uber is worth $141 billion.

Shares of Uber fell 3.7%, while DoorDash dropped 3.8%. Instacart stock had risen 15% this year before today.

An Instacart spokesperson declined to comment to Seeking Alpha. DoorDash and Uber didn't immediately respond to an email request for comment.

Instacart (CART) is set to report Q3 results on Nov. 5.

data.title: Middle East physical oil prices are falling while Brent crude soars to six-month highs
data.description:
Physical prices of some Middle East crudes sold outside the Persian Gulf reportedly have dropped in recent days, as more cargoes are pushed through the Strait of Hormuz in ship-to-ship transfers offshore Oman and producers offer competitive prices to Asian buyers.

Among examples of the shift, a cargo of Iraqi Basrah Medium crude was sold at a discount of nearly $10/bbl to the physical Dubai benchmark on a ship-to-ship transfer basis in the Gulf of Oman, after the crude grade was offered at near parity to Dubai a month ago, traders told Bloomberg.

The premium of Oman crude over Dubai, the leading Middle East measure of market strength, fell this week to the lowest level since the end of July, according to OilPrice.com, after the differential had surged to as high as $65/bbl in March.

The higher availability is depressing the prices of various physical crude grades from the Middle East, which come with assurances of an ability to get oil out of the Gulf, and are in contrast with trends in global benchmark oil futures, with front-month Brent contracts rising for five consecutive weeks and settling at six-month highs on Friday.

"The move higher in oil futures is not fundamentally driven at the moment; instead the market is trading supply risks," ING's head of commodities strategy Warren Patterson said in a note.

"While Middle East flows are holding up well for now, the real concern for the market is how sustainable these would be with renewed attacks, which helps to explain the divergence between the paper and physical market," Patterson said.

Meanwhile, a tanker carrying Russian diesel is heading to the U.S., Reuters reported Friday, following the agreement reached this month between the two countries.

The Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes ​was loaded with 40K metric tons of ultra-low sulfur diesel in the Russian Baltic port of ​Primorsk on October 22 and is expected to arrive in the U.S. on November 7, according to the report.

The cargo will be the first ​imported by the U.S. since former President Biden announced a ban on U.S. imports ​of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022.

Crude oil futures rose Friday, closing out the week with strong gains on fears of escalating conflict in the Middle East driven by Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and increasing talk about renewed U.S. military strikes against Iran.

"Crude oil prices are on the rise as the market rebuilds geopolitical risk premium amid escalatory rhetoric from the U.S.-Israel and Iran, raising fears of renewed and potentially even more intense back-and-forth strikes," Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note.

"The market is concerned about the continued Iranian attacks on tankers that we've seen increase over the last week," according to Lipow Oil Associates president Andrew Lipow. "While there has been an increase in oil transiting out of the Strait of Hormuz, that could change at any minute."

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery rallied 3.8% to $103.27 and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for December delivery surged 3.1% to $116.72/bbl, its highest settlement value since April 29.

Front-month Nymex ULSD (HO1:COM) for November delivery gained 1% on Friday to $4.9482/gal, while front-month Nymex RBOB November gasoline (XB1:COM) added 1.1% to $3.2116/gal.

For the full week, Nymex jumped 4.3%, Brent crude climbed 6.2%, its fifth consecutive weekly gain, and ULSD rose 1.7%, its fourth straight weekly gain, but RBOB gasoline slipped 0.7%.

U.S. natural gas futures (NG1:COM) extended the week's steep losses as mild weather for the time of year combined with rising production; the front-month Nymex November contract fell 5.6% on Friday to $2.640/MMBtu, concluding the week's 15.3% plunge.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), rose 1.6% this week.

data.title: Dr. Reddy’s outlines semaglutide relaunch in November 2026 and reiterates 6M-7M devices target
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited (RDY) Q2 FY '27

Management View

  • CFO Mannam Venkatanarasimham reported, "The business reported a 1.5% year-over-year decline in revenue, while EBITDA margin was at 20.6% for the quarter," adding, "Consolidated revenue stood at INR 8,671 crores, which is USD 905 million," and "Diluted EPS for the quarter is at INR 11.1."

  • CEO Erez Israeli said, "We remain consistent with -- in our strategic priorities of delivering double-digit growth across geographies and sustainable profitability," and tied Q2 margin delivery to execution: "We achieved an EBITDA margin of 20.6%, supported by the strength of our base business and our continued efforts to drive productivity."

  • On semaglutide recovery, CEO Israeli stated, "Subject to successful validation, we expect to relaunch semaglutide both directly as well as through our partners in November 2026," and emphasized continued pipeline progress: "We also remain focused on advancing abatacept and other complex generics as they move through the regulatory review process in the coming quarters."

  • CEO Israeli highlighted multiple partnerships and approvals, including, "We partnered with Takeda to bring India's first approved dengue vaccine, we call it QDENGA, to the private markets in India in the first half of 2027," and, "We received U.S. FDA approval for rituximab biosimilar, which will be commercialized in the U.S. through our partners, Fresenius Kabi."

  • In segment performance commentary, CEO Israeli said, "Our North America generic business reported revenue of $264 million for the quarter," and described launch activity: "During the quarter, we launched 6 new products, including first-to-market launch of sugammadex injection."

Outlook

  • On semaglutide demand and restart mechanics, CEO Erez Israeli said, "I'm very confident. And the confidence is based on orders that we already have," while noting gating items: "We still need to have the results of the validation. So this is still pending but I'm confident that it will be successful. And then we are ready to launch."

  • CEO Israeli reiterated volume targets and longer-run planning: "You've talked about we are still adhering to our guidance of 6 million to 7 million devices this year," and, "the run rate of 12 million to 15 million pens that we discussed in the past is still my estimate... take it as a very tentative number."

  • On gross margin framing, CFO Mannam Venkatanarasimham said, "we want to be, gross margin in the range of 50% to 55%," and CEO Israeli added directionally, "It will only go better from here."

  • On R&D intensity, CFO Venkatanarasimham guided, "coming quarters, what we believe our R&D is going to be in the range of 7% to 8%."

Financial Results

  • CFO Mannam Venkatanarasimham detailed profitability and drivers: "Consolidated gross profit margin was at 52.1%," "The SG&A spend was at INR 2,808 crores," "The R&D spend was at INR 524 crores," and "The profit before tax was at INR 1,228 crores."

  • Cash and balance sheet items included, "Cash flow during the quarter was INR 171 crores," and "As of 30th September, we have a net cash surplus of INR 2,502 crores, which is USD 261 million."

  • On cost pressure persistence linked to geopolitics, CFO Venkatanarasimham said, "we have seen the increase in the -- on the 3 fronts," and quantified, "overall, it has an impact close to 100 basis points on the EBITDA... we believe... this trend will continue for Q3 and Q4 as well."

Q&A

  • Neha Manpuria, BofA Securities: asked if semaglutide resumption uses Dr. Reddy’s own API/partner and confidence vs prior guidance; CEO Erez Israeli replied, "The main issue was with our ability to scale up the API. This problem is solved and we shipped all the necessary API to our partner," adding, "Most of the quantities will go to Canada."

  • Neha Manpuria, BofA Securities: asked what drove gross margin improvement and if it is the bottom; CFO Mannam Venkatanarasimham said, "This improvement... is a combination of the new products and the business mix," and CEO Erez Israeli added, "And your assumption is correct" and "It will only go better from here."

  • Kunal Dhamesha, Macquarie: asked about a large INR 1,370 crores change in other assets/liabilities; CFO Venkatanarasimham said, "this SSA claim... the payments have happened this quarter," adding, "If you remember, $50 million what we have provided in the Q4 during this H1."

  • Kunal Dhamesha, Macquarie: asked drivers of U.S. sequential revenue and margin delta; CEO Erez Israeli said, "the main driver is actually the business mix," and added, "The second is... the U.S. is more profitable because of the contribution of the new product."

  • Damayanti Kerai, HSBC: asked why API shipped before validation and the validation sequence; CEO Israeli explained, "you need now to do validation on the drug products using that API... about 3 weeks," and added, "you have basically validation in each stage."

  • Damayanti Kerai, HSBC: asked semaglutide approvals expansion; CEO Israeli said, "The right number is now 89 markets," and "Some of the approval in some other markets got delayed because of the scale-up as we needed to ship them samples."

  • Damayanti Kerai, HSBC: asked NRT recovery timing; CEO Israeli said, "it's -- the comparison year-over-year will be until we will finish the year," and, "The profitability is way above the expectations that we put in the business model."

  • Tausif Shaikh, BNP Paribas: asked abatacept update; CEO Israeli said, "We are still waiting for the EIR to come," and, "the goal date is indeed December 22 and we are hoping for an approval."

  • Foram Parekh, BOB Capital Markets: asked Europe growth trajectory and NRT; CEO Israeli said, "The next quarter should be better," and, "as for Europe, I'm expecting growth but it will not be significant growth this year," adding, "Ex-NRT Europe... should grow probably single digit this year."

  • Vishal Manchanda, Systematix: asked rituximab Europe market share and capacity; CEO Israeli said, "We have a single digit of market share in Europe," then clarified, "Low single digits," and added, "we were constrained by capacity."

  • Vivek Agrawal, Citi: asked abatacept market share potential and approval risk; CEO Israeli said, "a fair market share can be any number from 15% to 25%," and cautioned, "If you ask me, is there a chance that we'll get a CRL, there is a chance."

  • Aman Vij, Astute Investment: asked semaglutide launches in Brazil and other markets; CEO Israeli said, "Brazil likely in Q4, the beginning of Q4," and, "Some of it may come to the markets in Q3, some will come in January."

  • Saion Mukherjee, Nomura: asked PSAI/CDMO growth and $100 million-plus revenue mix; CEO Israeli said, "Our CDMO business under Aurigene Pharmaceutical Services generated revenues over $100 million in the last 12 months," and projected, "I believe that this business should grow and should reach 2 to 3x of these numbers in the next 3 to 4 years."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing on execution risk and sustainability, reflected in repeated probing on semaglutide restart, margins, and abatacept approval risk (e.g., "how confident are we of meeting the guidance" and "any possibility of getting CRL").

  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more assertive in Q&A, with CEO Erez Israeli stating, "I'm very confident," and reinforcing margin ambition: "we're actually aiming for the famous 25%."

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s focus on disruption and provisions, the current call’s tone shifted toward normalization and relaunch readiness, with CEO Israeli saying semaglutide timing is "consistent with the time lines communicated earlier," versus Q1’s emphasis on semaglutide-related margin drag and remediation.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Profitability language tightened from Q1’s reported "EBITDA margin of 12.5%" (including semaglutide-related provision) to Q2’s reported "EBITDA margin was at 20.6%," alongside management’s repeated references to mix and cost control as margin supports.

  • Semaglutide narrative progressed from Q1 planning to "resume semaglutide commercial supplies by November" to Q2 stating, "we expect to relaunch semaglutide... in November 2026," while remaining contingent on validation.

  • Business mix commentary sharpened in Q2, with CEO Israeli pointing to higher-profit geographies: "India, EM and the NRT... went to 53%," compared with Q1’s greater emphasis on disruptions (semaglutide provision, Middle East freight/solvents) as primary drivers.

Risks and Concerns

  • CEO Erez Israeli flagged remaining execution risk on semaglutide restart: "We still need to have the results of the validation. So this is still pending."

  • CFO Mannam Venkatanarasimham cited cost headwinds tied to geopolitics and logistics: "elevated freight costs due to supply chain disruptions arising from the Middle East crisis," and said the trend should persist: "we believe... this trend will continue for Q3 and Q4 as well."

  • On abatacept outcome uncertainty, CEO Israeli said, "It's obviously in the hand of the U.S. FDA," and separately added, "there is a chance" of a CRL.

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q2 as a margin-recovery quarter driven by base-business growth and mix, while positioning semaglutide for a November 2026 relaunch pending validation and keeping the 6 million to 7 million device target intact. Leadership also emphasized near-term biosimilar milestones (rituximab U.S. approval via partner and abatacept awaiting a December 22 goal date), while acknowledging ongoing risk from validation timing, U.S. FDA outcomes, and continued cost pressure from Middle East-related inputs and logistics.
